name: Anantara Villa Padierna Palace
positioning: Palatial golf resort, officially Anantara Villa Padierna Palace Benahavis Marbella Resort, in Andalusia's Golf Valley between Marbella, Benahavis and Estepona
best_for: Golfers who want a resort surrounded by three golf courses
Travelers who love art-filled, palace-style interiors and a Roman-style spa
Couples wanting a private pool villa

facts.text: The resort is set in Andalusia, between Marbella, Benahavis and Estepona in the south of Spain.
The resort is in the Golf Valley and is accessible from Malaga Airport.
The resort is surrounded by three golf courses.
The resort has a private racquet club and a thermal spa.
The resort has a beach club where guests can dine on fresh seafood.
La Loggia offers a quiet dinner atmosphere, and the Pergola serves snacks by the pool.
Rooms are set around central courtyards.
Connecting and family rooms are available.
The building is ochre-pink, and its interior is filled with paintings, sculptures and tapestries.
The resort has six meeting rooms and an amphitheater.

highlights.text: The property was once a stately home belonging to the Count of Villa Padierna.
The grounds include a lake, a Roman amphitheatre and more than 1,200 original works of art.
The Roman spa offers hydrotherapy, a hammam and aromatherapy rooms.
Private pool villas feature terracotta, marble statues and views of the amphitheatre.
The By The Sea Beach Club serves paellas, local espetos and cocktails while you watch the Mediterranean sunset.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes the resort is about a half-hour drive from the center; it is 12 km from Puerto Banus.
Parking is available for an additional daily fee.
WhataHotel notes the expansive resort layout requires walking or shuttle transport.
